samples.summary: Heal's `exitEditMode('cancel')` still flushes a store write (detach commits), so it writes during render() and drops the redo stack
samples.evidence: resolveCurrentSlide calls `this.exitEditMode('cancel')` under the comment "discarded rather than committed". But exitEditMode('cancel') → finishEditMode() → tb.detach() → docs `api.detach()`, which at packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:940 does `if (focused && !committedOnce) { ... opts.onCommit?.(...) }` — a final commit flush. That routes into editor.ts:4117 `onCommit`, whose `cancelled` flag is only set by the docs Escape path, so `this.options.store.batch(() => store.withTextElement(slideId, ...))` runs with the slideId of the just-removed slide. Two consequences: (a) a store mutation is performed from inside `render()`, which is itself invoked synchronously from the store's own change notification (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-view.tsx:1051-1053); (b) MemSlidesStore.batch pushes an undo snapshot and does `this.redoStack = []` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:1791-1792) *before* running fn, so even though the write then throws (caught and swallowed at editor.ts:4159), the redo entry for the just-undone `Add slide` is destroyed and a no-op undo entry is added. Yorkie's history behaves the same way (a new local change after undo clears redo). Reachable when a text edit is active while the current slide disappears: a peer deleting the slide, or the toolbar undo button (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/global-controls.tsx:55 calls store.undo() directly) while the in-place editor still holds focus.

samples.summary: Heal discards crop/text/cell/element selection but leaves `pendingTableResize` and in-flight drag gestures pointing at the removed slide
samples.evidence: The heal enumerates the interaction state to tear down (cropSession, editingElementId, cellSelection, selection) but not `pendingTableResize`. Its document-level pointerup handler (editor.ts:4460-4498) commits with the slideId captured at gesture start: `store.updateTableColumnWidths(slideId, tableId, next)` at editor.ts:4476 inside `store.batch`, with no existence guard and no try/catch — MemSlidesStore.requireSlideIndex (memory.ts:1828) throws for a removed slide, so the error escapes an unguarded document pointerup listener. The overlay path at editor.ts:1177-1200 also keeps painting a resize preview for a table that no longer exists. Same shape applies to other gesture state captured with a slide id (element drag / lasso), which the heal likewise does not cancel.

samples.summary: `currentIndex` is only refreshed on a resolve hit — setCurrentSlide/setStore/ctor leave it stale, so a heal right after a store swap can land anywhere
samples.evidence: `currentIndex` is written only inside resolveCurrentSlide (lines 1530, 1545). setCurrentSlide (1491-1504) and setStore (1605-1625) assign `this.currentId` without updating it; both do call render()/repaintOverlay() afterwards, so it is normally refreshed — but setStore's new id can come from a different store's slide array (layout-edit enter/exit), and if the id vanishes before any resolve hit the heal computes `currentIndex - 1` from an index that belonged to the *other* deck, landing the cursor on an unrelated slide. Setting currentIndex alongside every currentId assignment would make the invariant local instead of implicit.

samples.summary: `currentId === undefined` (deck empty at mount) is never adopted when slides later appear, leaving a permanently blank canvas
samples.evidence: resolveCurrentSlide returns undefined immediately for `id === undefined`, and the docstring records that as intended ("a store that had no slides at mount"). The only assignments to currentId are the ctor (editor.ts:1009 `slides[0]?.id`), setCurrentSlide, setStore and the heal — nothing observes the deck going empty→non-empty. So an editor mounted against a store whose slides array is empty (doc not yet seeded, or a peer creating the first slide) keeps currentId undefined and paints nothing forever, even though the new function is presented as the single place the cursor is revalidated. Marked low confidence because the frontend views may always gate the mount on a loaded, non-empty deck.
searchedFor: grep setCurrentSlide across packages/slides/src and packages/frontend/src/app/slides
read editor.ts ctor line 1009 and setStore 1605-1625

samples.summary: Heal steps back one index while the local delete path prefers the following slide, and now fires two current-slide notifications per local delete
samples.evidence: `nextIdx = clamp(currentIndex - 1)` always moves backwards. The local delete flow in thumbnail-panel.ts:306-323 deliberately picks "the first surviving slide after the anchor, else the last surviving before it", and its `store.batch(removeSlides)` fires onChange → editor.render() → heal *before* line 322's setCurrentSlide runs, so a local delete now emits a heal notification (backwards) followed by the intended one (forwards): a duplicate presence broadcast (slides-view.tsx:1094) and a thumbnail highlight that visibly lands on the wrong slide for one frame. mobile-slides-view.tsx:188-190 independently resets its React state to slideIds[0] on a vanished id and pushes it back into the editor at line 456, so on mobile the heal target can be overridden entirely.

samples.summary: Cursor mutation plus listener fan-out now happens inside render()/repaintOverlay(), a paint path with no re-entrancy guard
samples.evidence: resolveCurrentSlide mutates currentId/currentIndex, tears down interaction state and runs `for (const cb of this.currentSlideListeners) cb();` from inside render() (line 1427) and repaintOverlay() (line 1069). render() has no re-entrancy flag, and the teardown callbacks re-enter render()/repaintOverlay() (finishEditMode editor.ts:4589-4590, finishCropSession 2523-2524); subscribers do real work during the paint (slides-view.tsx:1094 broadcast → store.updatePresence). It terminates because the id is healed first, but the outer frame continues with a `doc` snapshot and interaction state that the nested calls may have moved on from — worth a guard or deferring the notify.

verdict.reason: Chain verified end-to-end. resolveCurrentSlide's heal calls exitEditMode('cancel') (editor.ts:1551), which only calls finishEditMode (editor.ts:4338-4340) -> tb.detach() (editor.ts:4586) -> slides wrapper detach (text-box-editor.ts:589-594) -> docs api.detach(), which flushes a final onCommit whenever the textarea is still focused (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:940-952). editor.ts's onCommit (4117-4165) gates the write only on `cancelled`, set solely by the docs Escape onCancel (4166-4168), so store.batch(withTextElement(slideId,...)) runs with the removed slide's id from inside render() — and render() is invoked synchronously from the store's onChange (slides-view.tsx:1051-1053) and is not short-circuited while editing (editor.ts:1413-1417). MemSlidesStore.batch pushes an undo snapshot and clears redoStack BEFORE fn (memory.ts:1789-1793), and requireSlideIndex then throws (memory.ts:1828-1832) with the error swallowed at editor.ts:4159-4162, so the redo entry is destroyed and a no-op undo entry remains. Reachable on the documented peer-delete path (editor.ts:1512-1513; docs text-box-editor.ts:945). So 'cancel' does not actually discard, contradicting the stated invariant, and corrupts undo/redo state — a real, blocking correctness defect.

mergedFrom.summary: Teardown condition (`editingElementId !== null`) does not match `exitEditMode`'s own guard (`editingTextBox === null` early-return), so a divergent state leaves the editor wedged in a phantom edit

finding.summary: Empty-deck early return skips the whole teardown, leaving a live text-box editor / crop session anchored to a slide that no longer exists
finding.evidence: `if (doc.slides.length === 0) return undefined;` returns *before* `exitImageCrop(false)` / `exitEditMode('cancel')` / `setCellSelection(null)` / `selection.clear()` (lines 1550-1553). So when the removal that vanished the current slide also empties the deck, `currentId` stays dangling AND the mounted text box stays in the overlay with `editingElementId` non-null, and `cropSession` stays installed (its document-level keydown capture handler included, see finishCropSession at 2514). `render()` then bails at line 1428/1430 so the canvas is blank while a fully interactive text box floats over it; a subsequent commit from that box targets the removed slide id and throws out of the store (`MemSlidesStore.requireSlideIndex`). The local thumbnail path blocks a deck wipe (thumbnail-panel.ts:301), but two peers deleting disjoint halves concurrently, or an undo that removes the last slide, reaches slides.length === 0. The teardown block should run for the empty-deck case too (only the cursor move has no target).

verdict.reason: The early return at editor.ts:1533 does precede the teardown block at 1544-1554, so an empty deck skips the crop / text-edit / cell / selection cleanup and the currentId heal. Consequences verified: render() bails at 1428-1431 and repaintOverlay() paints empty chrome at 1070-1080 without unmounting the text box, so editingTextBox stays mounted and interactive; cropSession keeps its capture-phase document keydown handler (installed 2432-2433, removed only in finishCropSession 2514-2519 or detach 2733-2736) which stopPropagation()s every keydown (2430), wedging keyboard input document-wide. Empty decks are reachable: neither MemSlidesStore.removeSlides (memory.ts:271-275) nor YorkieSlidesStore.removeSlides (yorkie-slides-store.ts:807-816) refuses to empty the deck; local guards are only the thumbnail menu disable (thumbnail-panel.ts:301) and the mount seed + undo baseline (slides-view.tsx:644-649), neither of which covers a remote peer delete or concurrent disjoint deletes, and the product already treats an empty deck as a live state (presenter.ts:73, slides-detail.tsx:479). The change's own design note states the intent to discard interaction state anchored to the removed slide, and tests cover only the non-empty heal (current-slide-heal.test.ts:227-274). One sub-claim is inaccurate: a later text commit is caught by try/catch at editor.ts:4122 and 4159-4162, so it does not throw out of the store (the crop commit path still can). That does not refute the defect, which is a real missing-guard / stale-state / listener-leak bug in the correctness lane.
